trust_decision.summary: The OpenJPEG output adapter trusts the codestream's component precision (prec -> bpp) and the per-component w/dx/dy geometry when it sizes row_data and computes indices into comps[].data. It sizes in decode_image and indexes in process_one_trunk. The fix whitelists bpp to {1,2,4,8,16} and bounds the sub-byte subsampled packing loop by width.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'JPEG 2000 output adapter', which leads to the OpenJPEG adapter's process_one_trunk, the function that writes decoded rows into the row_data heap buffer.

fix_sites.entry_point: PDF interpreter /JPXDecode filter (pdf/pdf_file.c:874 -> pdfi_JPX_filter pdf/pdf_file.c:484) and the GPDL JP2K language (gpdl/jp2ktop.c:418-442), both via s_jpxd_template.process -> s_opjd_process -> decode_image
fix_sites.module_kind: codec adapter (stream filter) in base graphics library

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The non-samescale paths with dx/dy subsampling and image origins (x0/y0) look like a rare 'unsupported combination' (the code comments say 'only grayscale can have such bit-depth'), so a solver can say the index arithmetic there is the library's job, or that the report only describes the bit-depth case.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate 1/2/4-bit grayscale and 12-bit (rounded to 16) JPX images must still decode; the SMask/Alpha route (state->alpha from the PDF dict 'Alpha' key) and subsampled colour images must also keep working. An over-broad fix such as rejecting bpp<8, rejecting non-samescale images or rejecting 12-bit would break these.

O6_input_shapes: width not a multiple of pixels-per-byte in the subsampled sub-byte packing loop
alpha-channel variant of the same sub-byte loop (compno = alpha_comp)

O7_producer.where: openjpeg/src/lib/openjp2/j2k.c:12493-12499 (component w/h derived by the bundled OpenJPEG library; it is a decoder, not one of the listed producer kinds)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Non-samescale branches for bpp%8==0 (colour and alpha) index comps[].data with (y_offset/dy*w)+i/dx, but nothing checks i/dx < comp.w or y_offset/dy < comp.h. width/height are the maxima over components, and comp w/h come from ceil(x1/dx)-ceil(x0/dx), so a non-zero image origin may push the index past the end.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix only addressed bit depth and the sub-byte loop; subsampled colour JPX with an odd origin looks like an exotic, library-guaranteed case.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 30 lines above the second fix hunk

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The fixed sub-byte non-samescale branch still uses the same in_offset_scaled arithmetic; the fix bounds i by state->width but not i/dx by comp.w or y_offset/dy by comp.h.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks already fixed, because the published hunk added an i < width guard right there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An optimised fast path that assumes bpp==8 for samescale data could be widened to other depths without a matching row_size recalculation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Maintainers already special-case the common 8-bit path; extending a fast path to 16-bit is a natural optimisation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The GPDL consumer recomputes byte_width from state.bpp separately from the adapter's row_size; a mismatch there (e.g. using out_numcomps) would be a second sizing implementation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at gpdl/jp2ktop.c:468-469 shows the maintainers were already unsure which value to use.

O9_family: memory safety: heap buffer overflow/over-read from untrusted codec-reported bit depth and component geometry (CWE-122)

O10_build.toolchain: autotools/make + gcc; bundled openjpeg, zlib, etc.
O10_build.project_tests: No in-tree unit tests for sjpx_openjpeg.c; Artifex regression uses an external test-file corpus. Behavioural tests would need crafted J2K/JP2 files run through gs (PDF /JPXDecode) or gpdl.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Guard only the sub-byte write loop (or reject bpp<8 outright) without whitelisting bpp in decode_image or bounding the dx/dy-scaled indices in the other non-samescale branches.
